summary: POC scoping focused on defining latency and throughput SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), workload sizing and an actionable measurement plan. Customer requires p95/p99 targets for both interactive queries and batch re-rank workloads, with timeline for a 3-week POC and a follow-up bench run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Rosie Alvarez (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Rahul Mehta, Dana Cho, Evan Park (Novus Analytics)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off — this is Maya from Redwood, with Samir our SE, Rosie on CSM. quick agenda: scope latency slos, TTFT vs TPOT, figure out success criteria and timeline.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: great, hi all. our ask is pretty straightforward: we want to validate that the model can meet our interactive query p95 under 150ms and not blow up cost. we also have a batch re-rank job that needs high throughput.
[00:25] Samir Patel: ok that's helpful — when you say interactive queries is that web UI low-QPS or internal API?
[00:30] Evan Park: mostly web UI, ~120 RPS peak across region, median payload ~512 tokens, often shorter. also occasional spikes to 350 RPS for a few minutes.
[00:40] Rahul Mehta: and our batch re-rank runs nightly, about 200k items, throughput target is tokens/sec oriented, we measure TPOT as tokens per second end-to-end from request to model output.
[00:52] Maya Chen: awesome, quick defs so we're aligned: TTFT = time to first token, that measures cold-start + generation latency to first token; TPOT we sometimes see called TPT (time per token) or tokens/sec — for this POC we'll record both TTFT and per-token latency and compute derived tokens/sec. we usually report p50/p95/p99 across those metrics.
[01:10] Dana Cho: can you talk about what counts in TTFT? like network, prefix cache, warm KV cache?
[01:16] Samir Patel: good question — our canonical TTFT includes total server-side processing: request ingress, routing, model forward to first output, includes any KV cache hit cost. network time to client is separate but we can measure end-to-end if you want. there may be minor transcription issues — we call KV cache "KV cash" in older notes, sorry.
[01:32] Lena Ortiz: no worries. what's realistic for p95 targets? we said 150ms p95 — is that feasible?
[01:37] Samir Patel: it depends on model size and deployment mode. Hosted API with smaller quantized model can hit ~100-130ms TTFT p95 for short contexts on A100-like infra if your median sequence length is low. For 512 token median, TTFT includes initial generation and can be higher — also if you want p99, add 20-40% slack.
[01:55] Evan Park: our key customers expect p95 < 200ms for interactive. p99 ideally < 400ms but we're flexible. cost sensitivity is high.
[02:03] Maya Chen: ok noted. For batch re-rank we'll measure TPOT as end-to-end tokens/sec and also batch throughput in items/sec. our approach: run baseline on Redwood Hosted API, then run on Dedicated pool with same model and quantization to compare delta.
[02:20] Rahul Mehta: how do you handle prefix caching and warm KV cache in benchmarks? we don't want synthetic wins from a fully warmed cache only.
[02:27] Samir Patel: our measurement plan includes three phases: cold-start (empty cache) runs, warm-cache steady-state runs, and mixed traffic with bursty patterns from your provided trace. we'll instrument KV hit rates, cache warming time and include both cold and warm p95/p99.
[02:40] Lena Ortiz: good. what about TTFT vs TPOT for long-context answers where generation is long — we care about latency to first token more than end-to-end for UI snappiness.
[02:48] Samir Patel: yes, TTFT is the UI snappiness signal — we'll set success criteria around TTFT for interactive calls and throughput (items/sec and tokens/sec) for batch. recommended targets based on your numbers: interactive p95 TTFT <= 180ms, interactive p99 <= 400ms; batch TPOT >= 15k tokens/sec on Dedicated for your nightly job. but we'll validate in bench.
[03:10] Dana Cho: curious about measurement windows — over what timescale do you compute p95/p99?
[03:15] Samir Patel: good net: we compute p95/p99 over 5 minute sliding windows for steady-state, and overall distributions for the whole run. for p99 we flag outliers and also provide tail latency histograms.
[03:26] Rosie Alvarez: also capturing percent of requests violating the SLO is helpful for SREs — e.g., target < 1% > threshold at p95.
[03:33] Rahul Mehta: security — we will need SOC2 docs and proof of encryption at rest, KMS integration, SAML SSO for Redwood Private if we go that route. can you share those?
[03:42] Maya Chen: yes, we'll send SOC2, ISO summary and details on KMS/HSM integrations. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; Dedicated also has audit hooks.
[03:50] Lena Ortiz: timeline — we want a papered POC in 3 weeks: week 1 baseline and fit check, week 2 bench runs and parameter tuning, week 3 validation and report. realistic?
[03:58] Samir Patel: doable if we get traces and initial creds within 3 business days. baseline run on hosted API takes a day to setup; Dedicated bench requires reserved capacity scheduling — we can provision for the POC in 5 business days if approved.
[04:10] Evan Park: what's needed from our side to size the Dedicated pool?
[04:14] Samir Patel: ideally: representative traffic trace (timestamp, payload size, model variant), target concurrent sessions, median/90th sequence lengths, and any peak windows. with those we can simulate and recommend GPU count and instance types.
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: we'll provide 3 days of traces and the nightly batch config.
[04:30] Maya Chen: perfect. measurement plan bullets: 1) ingest your trace into our harness; 2) run cold-start suite (3 runs); 3) run warm steady-state (30 min runs); 4) run mixed traffic burst tests; 5) run batch re-rank throughput tests; 6) produce report with p50/p95/p99 TTFT and per-token latency and tokens/sec plus cost per 1M tokens.
[04:52] Dana Cho: can you capture cost-per-query breakdown? we need token-level cost and infra cost split.
[04:56] Samir Patel: yes our Redwood Console exports token-level cost and per-route breakdowns. we'll include estimated per-1M-token cost for each config. there will be some variance across quantization and batch sizes.
[05:06] Rahul Mehta: on metrics collection what agents or instrumentation do you require on our side?
[05:10] Samir Patel: none initially for hosted; for Dedicated we'll ask for graceful ingress configs and allowlist IPs; we can ingest traces offline. if you want end-to-end network measured, a small client-side agent or synthetic runner is useful; otherwise we can do server-side-only measurements.
[05:22] Lena Ortiz: any gotchas about model variants and fallback? we might want cheaper LLM for low-criticality flows.
[05:27] Samir Patel: yep — smart routing lets us fallback to cheaper quantized model when capacity or cost constraints hit. important to measure quality/regression so we won't recommend fallback for flows that need exact quality. part of the POC is a small qualitative eval on 50 critical prompts to ensure rollbacks are acceptable.
[05:44] Maya Chen: let's capture success criteria explicitly: 1) interactive TTFT p95 <= 180ms and p99 <= 400ms in steady-state for representative traffic; 2) batch re-rank throughput >= 15k tokens/sec and complete nightly job within your window; 3) cost per 1M tokens <= your budget threshold (Dana to confirm number); 4) SSO/KMS and SOC2 docs provided.
[06:05] Dana Cho: we will confirm cost thresholds — internal procurement needs a number by early next week.
[06:09] Rosie Alvarez: I'll attach our POC doc and benchmark spreadsheet after the call.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: and how will you report TTFT vs TPOT differences? we want both in dashboard form and raw CSV.
[06:18] Samir Patel: we'll share dashboards in Redwood Console link and export CSV/JSON with per-request traces including timestamps, token counts, TTFT, per-token times. note that request IDs may be anonymized in hosted mode; Dedicated can keep your real IDs.
[06:31] Evan Park: what about warm cache sim? we have heavy reuse on prefixes — ensure benchmark includes realistic cache hit rates.
[06:36] Samir Patel: yes we'll replay your traces preserving session IDs to get realistic cache hit patterns. we'll also manipulate cache hit rate as a knob.
[06:45] Maya Chen: Alright last part — next steps recap: Maya to send POC doc + benchmark template, Samir to prep harness and propose measurement scripts, Rahul to send traces, Redwood to schedule bench run for dedicated pool pending approval.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: good, thanks everyone.
[07:01] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and put dates in calendar. bye.

End transcript.
